# GAPS — что спецификация явления НЕ содержит

*Machine-pinned inventory of the gaps in `phenomenon.py` / `holes.py`. Generated by `tests/gaps_report.py`; the preface and the Russian summary are hand-written. Regenerate with `python3 tests/gaps_report.py --write`.*

**What the specification claims.** `phenomenon.py` asserts that "integrality out of many weak constraints" is a *phenomenon*: a two-tier constraint system (STRONG lines `|ℓ| ≥ 2·cap+1`, WEAK lines `|ℓ| = cap+1`) in which no weighted sum of local constraints sees the truth, so `LP(all) − IP` is linear in `|V|`. It ships five principles P1–P5, six signatures S1–S6, a bestiary of eight analogous systems, one measured instance `OUR_SIGNATURE` (`4/4 признаков явления: ЯВЛЕНИЕ`), and three toy models. `holes.py` lists eight missing interactions H1–H8, each with a payoff. Both are appendices to `deep_research_brief_8`, whose questions Q1–Q7 are generated one per hole — so these two files are the object that external researchers are asked to reason from.

**What the tests establish it does not contain.** 198 tests, of which 36 carry `@gap`. A `@gap` is `unittest.expectedFailure`: the run stays green while the gap is open and turns RED the moment someone closes it without updating the spec. Every gap was verified twice — it fails at the assertion its docstring names (not at an import, a field-name preference, or an unrelated claim), and it *passes* against a simulated corrected specification, so none is a permanent xfail that could never go red. Two candidate gaps (`GAP-H-05`, `GAP-P-04`) were rejected on review as pedantic and demoted to ordinary tests; their numbers are retired, not reused.

**The three most consequential, ranked.**

1. **The diagnostic cannot detect its own subject.** `Signature` has no field for the integer optimum, so the integrality gap — the definition in §0 — is not representable at all; S2 measures `LP(all)/LP(strong)`, which is equally high when LP is blind and when there is nothing to be blind to. The consequences are executable, not rhetorical: a disjoint union of five-point blocks with `LP = IP = 2t` scores `4/4 … ЯВЛЕНИЕ`; the empty system scores `4/4`; arcs in `PG(2,q)` — the module's own example of a *solved, regular* system where it says the phenomenon is absent — score `3/4 … ЯВЛЕНИЕ` with three conditions satisfied vacuously; and cap sets in `F₃ⁿ`, the module's own paradigm of LP blindness, score `2/4 … не характерно`. False positive and false negative on the bestiary the module itself wrote. `Strength` has no third value and `verdict()` no third outcome, so "the phenomenon is absent here" is literally unsayable, and the claim "our problem is an instance of the phenomenon" — on which the whole transfer-of-mechanisms strategy rests — carries no information. `[C-02, C-03, F-03, F-05, P-05, P-06]`
2. **Two of the eight holes and one of the five principles are the target itself.** Computed from the inequalities the module prints: H4 (`|S₂| ≤ (3(p−1) − |S₁|) + O(1)`) sums to `3(p−1)+C` at every split, and H7 (`T(S) ≥ c(|S| − 3(p−1) − C)`) gives `3(p−1)+C` at `T = 0` for every `c > 0` — no loss in the constant, so H4 ⇔ H7 ⇔ target. The project's own notes say so verbatim (B.12: "not an intermediate hypothesis but the target itself in supersaturation form"; B.13: "any proof of it is a proof of T1"). P4 meanwhile asserts as an established *principle* precisely what H3 and H4 record as missing, and carries none of the hedging marks the module uses elsewhere. The brief ships H4 and H7 as fillable holes with "testable now" experiments and asks for a ranked list of the three most promising transfers: any answer to Q2 or Q5 is a complete solution of the open problem, so the difficulty calibration sent to outsiders is wrong. `[H-01, C-05, P-08]`
3. **The one signature that touches the integer truth is measured on a different system and carries no scale.** `gain_over_construction = (5,5,6,5)` is the per-`p` maximum over *all* `k` (notes B.6c), while `OUR_FRAME` fixes `xy ≡ ±1`, i.e. `k = −1`, whose maxima `32/40/54/59` give gains `(2,4,6,5)` — spread 4 against S4's threshold 3. Substituting the frame's own numbers turns the module's headline `4/4` into `3/4` on its own data. Worse, S4 is coded as an absolute spread over four points with no reference to system size, so a gain that is `Θ(|V|)` passes it and `t` disjoint copies of a fixed system fail it: the `O(1)` that *is* the project's target (`α ≤ 3(p−1) + O(1)`) is unfalsifiable in the very diagnostic meant to certify it. `[N-03, P-07, F-04, C-06, N-05]`

**Also missing, and directly actionable for a research agenda:** no hole corresponds to P1's transversal/packing reformulation — the container/entropy route is absent from all eight holes *and* from the brief (zero occurrences of container, Samotij, Saxton, Thomason, entropy), so it cannot come back through Q1–Q7 `[H-02]`; and all eight holes are upper-bound tools, with nothing on the lower-bound side although §6 lists `(T4)` as open and B.11 calls it "the next real step" `[H-04]`.

The k = −1 data are α = 32 at p=11 (§7 'p=11: 32–35' exact over all k; §4 lists k=2→33, k=3→35, k=−1→32), 54 at p=17 and 59 at p=19 (§2), i.e. gains 2, 6, 5 with a spread of 4 > 3; the entered first term 5 is exactly the k = 3 value 35 − 30. §7's own summary — 'for EVERY second hyperbola the gain over 3(p−1) is between +2 and +6' — gives the same spread of 4. With the frame's own numbers S4 is FALSE and OUR_SIGNATURE scores 3/4, the same as the decomposable blocks system of GAP-P-05. | S4 is the module's only quantitative claim about extremals, and the verdict '4/4 … ЯВЛЕНИЕ' printed by phenomenon.py's __main__ depends on it. With the project's own exact data our system scores no better than a system that splits into blocks of five, so the module's own numbers do not certify the phenomenon in the frame the module was written for. |
| `GAP-T-01` | the integer side of lp_blind_toy's 'gap' is a greedy heuristic, although the module itself computes the integer optimum exactly (P1 + its own tau solver) | §0 defines the phenomenon as the gap between the relaxation and the INTEGER OPTIMUM, P2 calls that gap 'суть явления', and lp_blind_toy is offered as its executable demonstration ('Показывает P2 в чистом виде') under a key literally named 'gap'. The integral side must therefore be alpha. The module even states how to get it — P1: 'max\|S\| = \|V\| − τ(H₃)' — and ships transversal_vs_fractional_toy, which computes τ exactly by brute force on the SAME generator (proved identical here), so alpha = n − τ is available inside the module for every instance the toy can handle. With no constraints at all (m = 0) LP* = alpha = n, so the gap must be exactly 0. | The integral side is one run of a greedy heuristic seeded by the same RNG. On the shipped default (30,200,0) greedy = 11 while a re-verified independent set of size 14 exists, so at least 3 of the 9 reported units are greedy failure; over seeds 0..19 the number swings 8..12 with the hypergraph size fixed. On (15,25,0) the module's own τ = 5 gives alpha = 10 and an honest gap of 0.0 where the toy reports +2.0; on (15,12,0) τ = 3 gives alpha = 12 and an honest gap of −2.0 where the toy reports +1.0; at m = 0 it reports −10.0. | P2 — the principle on which the project bases its central negative conclusion (LP is blind: covers plateau at LP(1) ≈ 3.45(p−1) and 11/3 → 115/32, so the covering route is closed) — has no executable witness. The one number the module labels 'gap' measures the failure of a greedy heuristic: it is positive on instances where the module's own exact route gives zero or a negative value, so its sign carries no information about integrality, and it does not grow with the size of the system, which is the phenomenon's defining scaling claim. |
| `GAP-T-02` | supersaturation_toy reports the MEAN over random subsets — a statistic that is provably independent of the hypergraph, so it cannot exhibit P3 at all | P3 is a universally quantified LOWER bound: for EVERY S with \|S\| > alpha + C, T(S) >= c(\|S\| − alpha − C); holes.py's H7 asks for exactly that lemma for the pair of hyperbolae. The quantity it constrains is min_{\|S\|=k} T(S). Any executable form of P3 — however crude — must therefore be a statistic that is 0 below the threshold and that changes when the hypergraph changes. | The toy returns the MEAN of T over 200 uniformly random k-subsets. For ANY 3-uniform hypergraph with m edges that mean is m*C(k,3)/C(n,3) — verified here numerically against the closed form and exactly on two hypergraphs with equal (n, m) whose minima differ (0 vs 1) while their exact means are identical. So the curve is positive at every k > 2 regardless of structure: on the toy's own instance a re-verified 16-element set with ZERO triples exists, yet the curve already reports 18.8 at k = 15. | The project's own data (pair_bound_notes B.12) give mean 53.5/51.5/71.5/118 against true minima 24/28/42/48 — a factor 1.7–2.5 — and B.12(iii) states outright that second-moment/'typical' bounds cannot reach the minimising orientations. The module's only executable illustration of supersaturation is precisely the statistic the project's own research rules out: it would report the same 'supersaturation' for a system that has none, so it makes H7 — the declared soft-form fallback route to 3(p−1)+O(1) — look automatically available. |
| `GAP-T-03` | no toy contains a STRONG constraint: the two-tier system whose interaction §0 uses to DEFINE the phenomenon is never instantiated | §0 defines the phenomenon as an interaction of two sorts of constraint — STRONG (\|l\| >= 2cap+1: rows, columns, slopes ±1) and WEAK (\|l\| = cap+1) — and asserts that the truth is fixed by the weak ones JOINTLY rather than by the strong ones; S2 states it quantitatively as LP(all) ≈ LP(strong). An executable model of that claim must contain both sorts of constraint, so that the two regimes can be compared at all. | All three toys build one and the same uniformly random 3-uniform hypergraph (proved identical here): every constraint has size 3 = cap+1, so Frame.strength classifies all of them WEAK and not a single STRONG constraint exists in any executable line of the module. Frame, OUR_FRAME, Strength and capacity are never read by any toy (instrumenting Frame.strength records zero calls); the signatures are (n, m, seed) and cap = 2 survives only as the literals 2/3 and 3. | Everything the module executes is compatible with 'uniformly random 3-uniform hypergraphs have integrality gaps' — true of systems with none of the project's structure (no algebraic extremals, no rich lines, no construction to exceed by O(1)). S2 and S6, the two signatures that carry the project's decision to abandon covers, are never measured, and the two signature conditions that ARE derivable from a constraint system are met by the toy's random hypergraph exactly as by ours (max codegree 6 in both). Nothing in the module distinguishes our system from a random one, and the claim that the weak constraints jointly decide the optimum is nowhere exercised by code. |
| `GAP-T-04` | no executable line of the module computes a fractional optimum: both 'fractional' slots are constants in n | P2/S2/S6 are statements about LP VALUES (τ*(H₃), LP(all)/LP(strong), the 3.45 plateau). The toys are the module's only executable content; lp_blind_toy reports a 'fractional' value and transversal_vs_fractional_toy reports 'n/3 (τ* upper bound)'. Whatever occupies those slots must be a property of the constraint system — at fixed n the packing LP optimum provably varies with the constraints (m = 0 gives exactly n, and any one triple already forces LP* <= n − 1) — and it must dominate the integer optimum. | Both slots are hard-coded constants, 2n/3 and n/3, depending on n alone. lp_blind_toy(30, m) returns 20.0 for m = 0, 50 and 200 alike, although with zero constraints the LP optimum is exactly 30, and a 3-uniform hypergraph with the same (n, m) = (30, 200) has LP optimum >= 26 (exhibited here, feasibility certified in exact Fraction arithmetic). On (15,12,0) the slot reads 10.0 while the module's own τ = 3 gives alpha = 12, so the 'relaxation' is strictly below the integer optimum. transversal_vs_fractional_toy prints 5.0 in the fractional slot both for the instance with τ = 5 and for the one with τ = 6. | The module asserts LP blindness as the heart of the phenomenon but never evaluates an LP, so nothing in it can tell a blind relaxation from a tight one, and S2 (LP(all) ≈ LP(strong)) and S6 (local certificates plateau) cannot be measured on any system at all. The project's quantitative claims — LP(1) ≈ 3.45(p−1), IP(1) = LP(1) − O(1), 11/3 → 115/32 — enter the specification as prose and are carried by no computation the specification can run, which is exactly what a reader would take the toys to have checked. |

A researcher answering Q2 of the brief is asked to import a stability/exchange mechanism in order to establish a property that phenomenon.py already lists as one of the five reasons the phenomenon happens; and any analogue can be 'matched' on P4 by assumption. Of the five principles, P1 is false as written, P3 is unfalsifiable, P5 keeps no falsifiable clause (see the tests above) — P4 is the fourth of the five, and it is a conjecture. |

## Краткое резюме (RU)

`phenomenon.py` объявляет «целочисленность из многих слабых ограничений» явлением и даёт его опознаватель: принципы P1–P5, признаки S1–S6, бестиарий из восьми аналогов, измеренный `OUR_SIGNATURE` с вердиктом «4/4 признаков явления: ЯВЛЕНИЕ» и три игрушки. `holes.py` перечисляет восемь недостающих взаимодействий H1–H8. Оба файла уходят приложениями к `deep_research_brief_8`, вопросы Q1–Q7 которого порождены по одному на дыру.

198 тестов, из них 36 с маркером `@gap`, фиксируют не то, что есть, а то, чего нет. Главное: **опознаватель не видит того, что опознаёт.** В `Signature` нет поля для целочисленного оптимума, поэтому разрыв интегральности — определение явления из §0 — в принципе непредставим; S2 меряет `LP(все)/LP(сильные)`, а это отношение одинаково велико и когда LP слепо, и когда слепнуть не на что. Отсюда исполняемые следствия: система из непересекающихся пятиблоков с `LP = IP` получает «4/4 ЯВЛЕНИЕ», пустая система — тоже 4/4, дуги в `PG(2,q)` (собственный пример модуля с точным ответом) — 3/4, а cap sets, его же образец слепоты LP, — «2/4 не характерно». У `Strength` нет третьего значения, у `verdict()` — третьего исхода: сказать «здесь явления нет» нечем, и вывод «наша задача — экземпляр явления» не несёт информации.

Второе: **две дыры из восьми и один принцип из пяти — это сама цель.** H4 и H7 по собственным формулам модуля заключают ровно `3(p−1)+C` без потери в константе (B.12: «не промежуточная гипотеза, а сама цель»; B.13: «любое её доказательство есть доказательство T1»), а P4 объявлен установленным принципом ровно там, где H3/H4 записывают нехватку. Значит калибровка сложности, отправленная внешним исследователям, неверна: ответ на Q2 или Q5 — это полное решение открытой задачи.

Третье: **единственный признак, касающийся целочисленной правды, измерен на другой системе и лишён масштаба.** Вектор `(5,5,6,5)` — максимум по всем `k`, тогда как рамка фиксирует `k = −1` с прибавками `(2,4,6,5)`; на собственных данных рамки вердикт падает с «4/4» до «3/4». А так как S4 закодирован абсолютным разбросом, прибавка порядка `Θ(|V|)` его проходит — то самое `O(1)`, ради которого всё делается, в опознавателе неопровержимо.

Отдельно: ни одна дыра не отвечает принципу P1 (маршрут «трансверсаль/контейнеры» отсутствует и в дырах, и в брифе), и ни одна не смотрит на нижнюю оценку, хотя §6 числит `(T4)` открытой.
